Description: Per-unit material costs including commodities, components, batteries (for EVs)
2024 Impact on EBIT: Higher for Ford Model e due to battery costs; Lower for Ford Blue with improving material costs; Ford Pro competitive mix advantages
Strategic Implications: Material cost management critical; battery costs declining with BlueOval SK ramping; commodity volatility major risk

Description: Per-unit warranty expense; higher for new vehicle launches (EV platforms) and quality issues
2024 Impact on EBIT: Ford Model e higher warranty burden due to new EV platforms; increased for Ford Blue with new launches; Ford Pro lower warranty costs relative to sales
Strategic Implications: Quality operations critical; EV platforms immature; recalls and defects create operational pressure (e.g., NHTSA consent order on rearview cameras)

Description: Per-unit freight and tariff costs; affected by global supply chain decisions
2024 Impact on EBIT: Inflationary pressure on logistics; tariff impacts on imports from Mexico and international operations
Strategic Implications: Global footprint creates logistics complexity; tariff uncertainty major risk (trade policy changes)

Description: Fixed manufacturing costs: hourly/salaried labor, plant overhead (utilities, taxes), new product launch expense, shift flexibility (overtime, line-speed, shift schedules)
2024 Impact on EBIT: Ford Blue: higher for maintaining large ICE portfolio; Ford Model e: high launch costs; Ford Pro: improving as Super Duty and Transit scale
Strategic Implications: UAW labor agreements impact costs; facility utilization critical; shift to EV requires manufacturing transformation

Description: Fixed engineering costs: vehicle/software engineers, prototype materials, testing, outside engineering services; critical for new platforms (EVs, software)
2024 Impact on EBIT: Ford Model e: very high due to new EV platform development; Ford Pro: high for software/services integration; Ford Blue: decreasing as platforms mature
Strategic Implications: Technology talent acquisition critical (hired from Apple, Tesla); autonomous/digital initiatives require ongoing investment

Description: Depreciation & amortization of manufacturing and engineering assets, asset retirements, operating leases
2024 Impact on EBIT: Increasing as capital expenditures on EV facilities and new technologies depreciate; major for BlueOval SK ramping
Strategic Implications: Capital intensity of EV manufacturing; depreciation accelerates with technology obsolescence

Description: Marketing and promotional costs including incentives, rebates, low-rate financing, stock adjustments
2024 Impact on EBIT: Ford Pro: lower per unit due to pricing power; Ford Model e: high due to competitive market/brand building; Ford Blue: stable baseline
Strategic Implications: Ford Pro's strong brand (F-150, Transit) reduces promotional need; EV market requires brand-building investment

Description: Salaried personnel costs for staff activities, IT services, selling functions; includes digital transformation investments
2024 Impact on EBIT: Increasing due to Ford+ digital transformation, cybersecurity investments, advanced data analytics (NHTSA consent order requirements)
Strategic Implications: IT infrastructure critical for competitive advantage; digital talent acquisition ongoing; cybersecurity investments required

Description: Foreign currency effects from international operations (especially Mexico, Europe, Turkey, China)
2024 Impact on EBIT: 2024: +$245M benefit; Ford Otosan in Turkey inflationary pressure; Mexico tariff/currency risks ongoing
Strategic Implications: Hedging programs in place; Turkish operations inflation exposure; tariff uncertainty major risk factor
